messages:
sam: Heads up — after the kernel-selection rollout last night I'm seeing a weird spike in our token latency cardinality on the perf dashboard. Not sure if it's label explosion or a real perf regression. @observability-bot can you dump the top 10 label combinations for token_latency_ms?
observability-bot: Here are the top 10 label tuples by series count for metric `token_latency_ms`: (route, model_family, kernel, quant_mode, batch_size)
1. /generate, llama2, kernel-3a, q4, 1
2. /chat, gpt-like, kernel-3a, q4, 1
3. /generate, llama2, kernel-3a, q8, 8
4. /embed, embedder-v1, kernel-3a, q4, 16
... (truncated)
maria: That list looks normal-ish, but note how `kernel` has many variants like `kernel-3a`, `kernel-3a-opt`, `kernel-3a-v2`. We probably need to canonicalize kernel naming rather than expose full git-ish refs as a label.
ajay: Agreed. Kernel-level labels should be low-cardinality. Suggestions: `kernel_name` (string, small set) + `kernel_hash` (not a label, but an annotation in logs) or `kernel_version` with semantic tags (e.g., "3a", "3a-opt").
leila: Also seeing `batch_size` as a label with values 1,2,4,8,16 — that's OK. But `route` is a freeform path; we currently have per-customer custom routes like `/acme/gen` which explode the cardinality. We should map route -> route_group label (e.g., generate, chat, embed) for metrics used in global dashboards.
sam: Proposed minimal label set for token latency:
- route_group (generate|chat|embed|rerank|other)
- model_family (llama2|gpt-like|embedder-v1|...)
- kernel (3a|3b|fallback)
- quant (q4|q8|fp16)
- batch_size (numeric but coarse: 1,2,4,8+)
- kv_hit (true|false)
maria: Love the route_group idea. For batch_size let's bucket it in telemetry: `1`, `2`, `3-8`, `9+` as string labels so Prometheus cardinality stays bounded.
devon: We also need to version the metric names rather than change label semantics silently. My recommendation: introduce `token_latency_ms_v2` while we migrate dashboards. That lets consumers opt-in and avoids breaking alerts.
ajay: +1 on explicit metric versioning. Also update histogram buckets to better capture low-latency tail. Current buckets are too coarse: [1,5,10,50,100,200,500] ms — needs [0.2,0.5,1,2,5,10,20,50,100,200,500].
leila: Quick question: where do we put kernel attributes that are runtime-specific (like `use_optimized_kernels=true`)? If we add a label for every toggle we'll blow up series. Maybe keep toggles out of metric labels and instead emit a `kernel_config` log event for debugging.
sam: Yes — keep metric labels to the small canonical set. Dump full runtime config to traces or logs with a correlation id. We can expose a `kernel_variant` label but only with a handful of stable values (default, opt, fallback).
maria: For dashboards: update per-route KPIs to use `route_group` and join with recent-deploy tags for rollout windows. Example PromQL for 95th token latency on generate routes:
```promql
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_ms_v2_bucket[5m])) by (le, route_group, model_family, kernel, quant, batch_bucket))
```
ajay: Note: `batch_bucket` is the bucketed batch_size label (1,2,3-8,9+). Also add `pv` tag for private vs hosted to split dashboards if needed: `deployment_tier` (hosted|dedicated|private).
devon: Migration plan outline:
1) Start emitting `token_latency_ms_v2` in parallel with current metric, mapping labels to canonical values (2 weeks).
2) Update Grafana dashboards and alerts to reference v2 (1 week overlap).
3) Deprecate `token_latency_ms` (announce 2 weeks, then remove) and keep logs/traces for debugging (one-month retention).
leila: Can we add an aggregator-side scrubber that maps `route` -> `route_group` before writing metrics? That will ensure older clients still work.
sam: Yes, implement scrubber in runtime telemetry emitter. Pseudocode for mapping rules:
```json
{
  "/generate": "generate",
  "/generate/*": "generate",
  "/chat": "chat",
  "/chat/*": "chat",
  "/embed": "embed",
  "default": "other"
}
```
maria: One more gotcha: label renames must be accompanied by a versioned tag in our ingest pipeline so downstream consumers can automatically switch if they want. Add `metric_schema_version` as a resource label (single small set) instead of renaming everything in-place.
ajay: I think `metric_schema_version` is fine as a resource label but keep it low-cardinality (v1,v2). Do NOT put the schema hash in every series.
observability-bot: Action items created: #OBS-312 (emit token_latency_ms_v2), #OBS-313 (implement route_group scrubber), #OBS-314 (dashboard migration). Links: https://redwood/obs/312
sam: I'll pick up #OBS-313. Plan to push scrubber as a small PR today, then wire it in the emitter config.
devon: I'll coordinate dashboard changes and set up a canary dashboard for v2 metrics. Will add a section showing both v1 and v2 side-by-side.
leila: For the rollout, let's also add a perf-regression smoke test: deploy kernel-3a to 1% of traffic and monitor `token_latency_ms_v2:95p` on generate routes. If > +20% from baseline, auto-fallback.
maria: Sounds good. One final ask — let's document label naming conventions in Observability docs (kebab-case, buy-in to route_group, no freeform ids). I'll add a short doc and link it to the ticket.
sam: Great. Thanks all. I'll post PR when scrubber is up. :rocket:
